result.target_topic: Financial effects of loan modifications for the year ended December 31, 2023
result.target_summary: For the year ended December 31, 2023, retained residential real estate financial distress modifications (FDMs) totaled $136 million. These modifications, predominantly term extensions and interest rate reductions, extended the weighted-average loan life by 20 years and reduced the weighted-average contractual interest rate from 7.21% to 4.44%.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures state that there were no additional commitments to lend to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty whose loans had been modified as FDMs. While D364 and D329/D330 discuss the specific financial effects/amounts for 2023, the 'no additional commitments' statement in D331 is the direct counterpart to the same statement in D364.

D364 describes the financial effects of 2023 FDMs and the lack of additional lending commitments. D330 restates the 2023 financial effects ($136M, 20 years extension, rate reduction) which matches D364's financial data. D331 states the no additional commitments, matching D364's commitment data. Thus, the 2023 disclosure D364 maps to both the restated 2023 data in D330 and the current 2024 commitment note in D331.

comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial loan modification program metrics (2024 vs 2023)
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, term extensions increased the weighted-average life of impacted loans by 1.7 years compared to 1.6 years in 2023, while the weighted-average duration of deferred payments was 9 months for both years; deferral periods typically ranged from 8 to 24 months.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose the financial effects of loan modifications for distressed borrowers, specifically focusing on term extensions and interest rate reductions. JPMorgan reported $136 million in retained residential real estate FDMs for 2023, where modifications extended the weighted-average loan life by 20 years and reduced rates from 7.21% to 4.44%. In contrast, Bank of America’s 2024 data for commercial loans shows term extensions increased weighted-average life by only 1.7 years, with a weighted-average deferral duration of 9 months. While both firms utilize similar modification mechanisms (term extensions, rate reductions), the magnitude of the term extension is vastly larger for JPMorgan's residential portfolio (20 years) compared to BAC's commercial portfolio (1.7 years).

sentences.text: For the year ended December 31, 2023, retained residential real estate FDMs were $136 million.

The financial effects of the FDMs, which were predominantly in the form of term extensions and interest rate reductions, included extending the weighted-average life of the loans by 20 years, and reducing the weighted-average contractual interest rate from 7.21% to 4.44% for the year ended December 31, 2023.
Term extensions granted increased the weighted-average life of the impacted loans by 1.7 years during 2024 compared to 1.6 years in 2023.
The weighted-average duration of loan payments deferred under the Corporation's commercial loan forbearance program was 9 months during 2024 and 2023.

comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley disclose policies regarding loan modifications for borrowers experiencing financial difficulties. JPMorgan’s 2023 residential real estate FDMs were predominantly term extensions and interest rate reductions. Similarly, Morgan Stanley states that it may modify loan terms for borrowers facing financial difficulties through interest rate reductions, principal forgiveness, and term extensions. While JPMorgan provides specific quantitative financial effects for its retained residential portfolio ($136 million, 20-year extension, rate drop to 4.44%), Morgan Stanley provides qualitative policy details without the same level of specific aggregate financial impact data for the period in the provided sentences.
